memory_candidates.content: To verify whether a Lean 4 program achieves genuine OS-thread concurrency (as opposed to deferred/serial execution that merely looks like Task scheduling), poll /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat's third field once per second against a COMPILED (not interpreted) build and count threads in the 'R' (running) state. A pure `Task.spawn (fun _ => expr)` closure can type-check and run correctly while never actually using more than one worker thread, including at `Task.Priority.dedicated` (which the Lean reference documents as always getting its own OS thread). Wrapping the same CPU-bound work in an `IO` action and dispatching via `IO.asTask` is what engaged genuine multi-thread concurrency on Lean 4.33.0-rc1. Useful whenever a synthetic concurrency probe produces a suspiciously flat or serialized measurement: check the spawn mechanism before concluding the underlying knob (e.g. LEAN_NUM_THREADS) doesn't work.

Lake has no mechanism of its own to cap concurrent build-job threads (no -j/--jobs flag; Lake 5.0.0 rejects both outright). Confirmed directly by Lake maintainer Mac Malone on the leanprover-community Zulip thread 'number of threads for lake build': Lean 'does not provide a way for user programs (like Lake) to limit the number of threads in its Task thread pool,' and LEAN_NUM_THREADS 'serves a good-enough fix for the few places this has been an issue.' The Lean reference additionally documents this pool size as 'not a hard limit; in certain situations it may be exceeded to avoid deadlocks.' A synthetic local probe using a flat, simultaneous multi-task fan-out (spawn N independent tasks, then wait on all from one caller) can show no observable capping effect under LEAN_NUM_THREADS even when the mechanism works in practice for a real, dependency-graph-driven job scheduler like Lake's doc-gen4 build -- the soft-limit escape valve is shape-sensitive, not necessarily a flat refutation of the variable's practical effectiveness.

sapience_notes.subject: Lean 4 Task.spawn pure closures vs IO.asTask concurrency
sapience_notes.value: On Lean 4.33.0-rc1, a pure Task.spawn (fun _ => expr) closure never observably uses more than one OS worker thread regardless of LEAN_NUM_THREADS, confirmed via /proc/<pid>/task/*/stat polling against a compiled binary, including at Task.Priority.dedicated. IO.asTask wrapping a CPU-bound IO action does achieve genuine multi-thread concurrency (8 threads simultaneously observed in the R state at LEAN_NUM_THREADS=8). A Lean concurrency probe should use IO.asTask, not pure Task.spawn, to get a meaningful signal.

sapience_notes.subject: Lake build-job concurrency control mechanism
sapience_notes.value: Lake has no mechanism of its own (no -j/--jobs flag; Lake 5.0.0 rejects both) to limit concurrent build-job threads; it relies entirely on the generic Lean runtime's LEAN_NUM_THREADS environment variable. Confirmed directly by Lake maintainer Mac Malone on the leanprover-community Zulip 'number of threads for lake build' thread: Lean 'does not provide a way for user programs (like Lake) to limit the number of threads in its Task thread pool,' and LEAN_NUM_THREADS 'serves a good-enough fix for the few places this has been an issue.'

sapience_notes.subject: Lean runtime Task thread pool soft limit
sapience_notes.value: The Lean reference documentation states the Task thread pool's configured size (via LEAN_NUM_THREADS, or defaulting to logical processor count when unset) 'is not a hard limit; in certain situations it may be exceeded to avoid deadlocks.' A synthetic probe that fans out many simultaneously-ready, non-nested tasks and waits on them from a single flat loop showed no observable capping effect at LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 on a 24-core host: 1433% CPU (unset) vs 1669% CPU (=1), via IO.asTask with 48 tasks.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic docs.yml API Documentation workflow OOM root cause and fix
sapience_notes.value: The doc-gen4 build OOM (error code 12, cannot allocate memory) in BimodalLogic's .github/workflows/docs.yml was growth-driven: FormalSystem/ grew from 705 to 772 .lean files while docs.yml and lean-toolchain stayed fixed, pushing ~6,300 doc-gen4 targets (each holding a full Mathlib+FormalSystem environment) past what 15 GiB RAM plus 15 GiB swap can hold concurrently. Swap enlargement alone (3 to 15 GiB) was measured insufficient (still 15 allocation errors). The fix applied: a step-level env: LEAN_NUM_THREADS: "1" on the docgen step, following leanprover/lean-action's own README precedent and opencompl/veir's production docs.yml for this exact failure mode. Verification requires a real pushed CI run (not locally reproducible); not yet confirmed green as of this task's completion.

sapience_notes.subject: GNU time on NixOS and bash's reserved time keyword
sapience_notes.value: A NixOS host may have no /usr/bin/time; GNU Time 1.10 is available via `command -v time` (resolving to /run/current-system/sw/bin/time), but bash's own reserved `time` keyword intercepts a bare `time -v cmd` and errors on the -v flag rather than invoking the real binary. Always invoke the resolved binary by its full path, or via `$(command -v time) -v ...`, to get GNU time's -v output instead of bash's builtin timer.
